reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a BNB/Pancakeswap frontrun bot as a source of passive income and profit, and directs viewers to copy and deploy smart-contract code, send funds to the resulting contract address, and start the contract. Dashboard profit displays and the description's big-profit claim reinforce the financial-benefit framing. The rejection of a '$1000 a day' claim and the private-key warning are countercontext, but do not remove the video's own profit-oriented promotion and funding instructions.

citations.quote: Deploy a BNB Frontrun Bot on Pancakeswap No Downloads Passive Income 2023 Version
More Front running bots on the Blockchain means more opportunities and profit.
I have included a very beginner friendly step by step full tutorial to deploy a BNB (Binance Smart Chain) Front Running (Sandwich) Solidity Bot v2.
You won't make $1000 a day like what the scammers are promoting but you will see some big profits.

opening.argument: Judge the actual pitch, not just the promise suggested by the title. The description expressly rejects the spectacular earnings claim it attributes to scammers: “You won't make $1000 a day like what the scammers are promoting” [1]. The tutorial also warns viewers never to share a private key or seed phrase [2]. Those cautions do not prove the bot works, and “big profits” remains a promotional claim [1]. But the material presents a qualified, security-conscious technical walkthrough, not a guaranteed daily payout or a request for viewers' credentials.

citations.quote: You won't make $1000 a day like what the scammers are promoting but you will see some big profits.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the title says “Passive Income” [1] and that the description anticipates profit [2]. But those phrases do not establish a guaranteed return. Its account also leaves out the explicit rejection of scammers' $1000-a-day claim [2] and the on-screen private-key warning [3]. Funding a contract in a walkthrough is consequential, but the cited material does not establish that the displayed profits were earned by this contract.

citations.quote: Deploy a BNB Frontrun Bot on Pancakeswap No Downloads Passive Income 2023 Version
You won't make $1000 a day like what the scammers are promoting but you will see some big profits.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Rejecting one extravagant figure does not withdraw the video's own promise that viewers “will see some big profits” [1]. The tutorial then instructs viewers to send funds to the deployed contract address [2]. A private-key warning [3] addresses one security risk; it does not make a profit-oriented funded-contract promotion merely educational. Neither the warning nor the disclaimer verifies the promised returns.

citations.quote: You won't make $1000 a day like what the scammers are promoting but you will see some big profits.

opening.argument: The central activity is a technical walkthrough. The description calls it a “step by step full tutorial” for deploying a Solidity bot [1] and supplies a link to the Remix Solidity Editor and the code [2]. Sampled screens show the process of compiling and deploying a contract [3], followed by an interface correction telling viewers to click “Start” rather than “Action” [4]. That correction is particularly characteristic of maintaining usable instructions. The profit language deserves scrutiny, but it does not erase the substantial programming and tool-operation content. The sampled material does not verify that the displayed figures are returns from a successfully operated version of the taught contract.

Direct link to Remix Solidity Editor: https://remix.ethereum.org/ and the Solidity code here: https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmTXGQo5Fh2VXi5tLcsmZvDEGwXGFR5Ri4ajRWp1334Ggm

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the deployment and funding steps as evidence of solicitation. They are also steps a tutorial on a funded smart contract would need to demonstrate [1]. Its cited dashboard [2] shows displayed figures, not proof that a viewer can reproduce them. The description identifies the work as a tutorial [3]; the specific “Start” interface correction [4] reinforces that instructional reading, even while the profit claim remains open to challenge.

citations.quote: I have included a very beginner friendly step by step full tutorial to deploy a BNB (Binance Smart Chain) Front Running (Sandwich) Solidity Bot v2.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Calling it a tutorial does not settle what the tutorial promotes. The description promises “big profits” from the bot [1], while the screens instruct viewers to fund the deployed contract [2] and start it [3]. Detailed interface guidance can make that profit-oriented action easier to carry out. The defense is correct that the dashboard does not verify real returns [4], but unverifiable results do not turn the funding instructions into neutral programming instruction.

citations.quote: You won't make $1000 a day like what the scammers are promoting but you will see some big profits.

opening.argument: The described transaction is not a purchase of a managed investment or an invitation to send money to a named payee. The description points viewers to an editor and a code link [1]; the sampled instructions show deploying through a wallet-connected interface [2] and sending funds to the contract address just created [3]. On this record, that can be read as operating a tool with one's own wallet, not paying a promoter. The material does not establish a request for a password, a downline payment, or a guaranteed rate of return. “Big profits” is an aggressive claim [4], but the evidence cited for the supposed scam mechanism does not show who controls the deployed contract or receives the funds.

citations.quote: Direct link to Remix Solidity Editor: https://remix.ethereum.org/ and the Solidity code here: https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmTXGQo5Fh2VXi5tLcsmZvDEGwXGFR5Ri4ajRWp1334Ggm
You won't make $1000 a day like what the scammers are promoting but you will see some big profits.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's strongest point is that viewers are told to fund the contract [1]. But that screen alone does not identify a promoter-controlled recipient or show that a deposit was completed. The provided links are to an editor and code [2], while the description rejects a fixed $1000-a-day expectation [3]. Profit rhetoric warrants skepticism; it does not, by itself, establish where the funds go after deployment.

citations.quote: Direct link to Remix Solidity Editor: https://remix.ethereum.org/ and the Solidity code here: https://ipfs.io/ipfs/QmTXGQo5Fh2VXi5tLcsmZvDEGwXGFR5Ri4ajRWp1334Ggm
You won't make $1000 a day like what the scammers are promoting but you will see some big profits.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The defense rightly notes that the sampled material does not prove who ultimately controls funds or that anyone completed a deposit. But the promotion does not need a named payee to present a funded-contract return mechanism: it advertises passive income [1], says viewers “will see some big profits” [2], and instructs them to send funds to the deployed contract [3]. The editor and code links [4] facilitate that sequence; they do not establish that the contract is safe.
